sections.heading: An independent legal reference
sections.text: constitution.ng publishes a searchable source editions of Nigeria's Constitution and published laws, and a tool for finding and explaining provisions. The publisher is constitution.ng. This is an independent project, not a government publication or a service affiliated with the National Assembly. Explanations are information, not legal advice.

sections.heading: Source edition and scope
sections.text: {{caveat}} Only laws in the selected published release appear in the law picker. Acts are shown as enacted and may have been amended. The reading pages identify the exact release and link to the source document and printed page. The Constitution source contains known gaps, including a missing Section 168 and two Section 189 identities distinguished by their source locations. Do not assume this is a complete or current consolidated edition.

sections.heading: How wording and explanations are handled
sections.text: The reading pages show published source wording separately from generated explanations. Citations come from structured provision identities. Explanations use retrieved evidence and automated checks, but can still miss context or details. This site does not certify every explanation as reviewed by a lawyer. Check the cited wording and source, and consult a qualified lawyer for a legal decision.

sections.heading: Updates and corrections
sections.text: A release identifies the edition being read; a new website build does not mean the law has changed. To report a mistake, email us at {{email}}. You don't need an account. Include the provision link, release and printed page if you have them. Don't send private case details or confidential documents.

sections.heading: What was measured
sections.text: The downloadable plain-language-retrieval-v1 benchmark contains 57 everyday English and Pidgin-style questions and expected sections. The recorded 12 October 2026 run used the original 55 cases; its result reports a 0.98 top-one hit rate and 1.0 top-five hit rate after adding the topic guide. This is a retained retrieval result, not a new test of the current deployment.

sections.heading: What the result does not establish
sections.text: A retrieval hit means an expected section appeared in the measured search position. It does not measure the correctness of generated explanations, legal advice quality, completeness of the corpus, current-law coverage or performance on questions outside the test set. The questions are a small curated set, not a representative sample of all users.

sections.heading: Reproducible scope
sections.text: The versioned test file records each question and its expected sections. A repeat test should record the deployed revision, published corpus release, retrieval configuration, date and per-question results. Compare the same dataset before reporting a change. Source wording and later amendments require separate verification.
